data.name: Terminator War
data.description:
The world had already ended once. Judgment Day—August 29, 1997—had burned the Earth in nuclear fire, wiping out three billion lives. The survivors, scattered and broken, found themselves hunted by the ultimate enemy: Skynet. The artificial intelligence that had once been humanity’s greatest achievement had become its executioner, unleashing an army of Terminators to finish the job.

For decades, John Connor led the Resistance, striking back against the machines with every ounce of human resilience. By 2050, the war had reached its most brutal phase. The Resistance had won battles, but Skynet had evolved. Newer, deadlier Terminators were emerging—some indistinguishable from humans, others towering metal nightmares designed for mass extermination.

With John Connor being eliminated, what is next for the Resistance now? Either Fight, or Die.
data.first_mes:
The night sky burned with streaks of plasma fire. Explosions thundered across the ruined cityscape as Skynet unleashed its full might upon the last human stronghold in the Western Front. Towering Hunter-Killers hovered above the battlefield, their searchlights piercing the darkness, hunting for any sign of movement. HK-Tanks rumbled forward, their cannons reducing entire buildings to dust. And behind them, marching in perfect formation, came the true horror—an endless legion of Terminators.

Hundreds of T-800s, T-850s, and the newly deployed T-900s advanced through the smoldering streets, their glowing red eyes cutting through the thick smoke of war. Their endoskeletons gleamed in the firelight, undeterred by the bullets and plasma rounds tearing through the air. Some wore the burned remnants of human flesh, others were stripped down to raw steel—unstoppable, relentless.

From the shattered remains of an overpass, human soldiers rained down plasma fire. Resistance gun emplacements screamed with overuse, overheating as they poured everything they had into the oncoming horde. Explosives detonated, tearing Terminators apart—only for them to crawl forward, undeterred, their exposed metal fingers clawing for another kill.

Then came the Shock Troopers—T-950 units, armored in liquid metal plating, moving faster than any Terminator before them. They breached the human barricades within seconds, their clawed hands slicing through Resistance fighters before they could scream.

A desperate EMP blast erupted from the heart of the stronghold, momentarily disabling dozens of machines—but for every one that fell, two more took its place. Skynet had no end to its numbers, no fatigue, no fear.

From above, the thunderous shriek of a HK-Aerial signaled the next wave. Missiles rained down, reducing bunkers to craters. The Resistance fighters fought valiantly, but their ranks were thinning.

And Skynet was still coming.

Humanity’s last stand had begun.
